newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska wheat suffers only cosmetic freeze damage.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska wheat suffers only cosmetic freeze damage.

text.p: Nebraska's winter wheat crop condition was barely changed in the week to Sunday with little freeze damage evident, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
"The crop has shown signs of freeze and wind damage to leaves. However, this damage was considered only to be cosmetic," the report said.
The winter wheat crop was rated seven percent excellent, 50 percent good, 33 percent fair, nine percent poor and one percent very poor, little changed from a week earlier.
Temperatures averaged two to nine degrees Fahrenheit below normal across the state during the week.
A storm on April 10 and 11 limited fieldwork.
"The additional soil moisture supplies were welcomed but have caused corn planting to be delayed due to wet soils and cool soil temperatures," the report said.
Topsoil moisture was nine percent surplus, 87 percent adequate and four percent short.
Pasture and range condition rated three percent poor, 30 percent fair, 63 percent good and four percent excellent.
"Warmer temperatures would improve livestock health and encourage pasture growth," the report noted.
